title: Florida's 20th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: Florida's 20th Congressional District, located in central Broward County, is the only solidly Democratic district in South Florida following the 2026 redistricting map enacted by Governor Ron DeSantis. The race features a contentious Democratic primary on August 18, 2026, with five candidates including U.S. Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (who currently represents the neighboring 25th district) facing four Black challengers who argue the seat should remain a stronghold for Black representation. The district has a Cook Partisan Voting Index of D+20, making the Democratic primary winner heavily favored in the November general election. The contest highlights national debates about racial representation, redistricting, and the future of the Democratic coalition in Florida.
polling_note: Limited public polling available. A May 2026 internal poll from the Wasserman Schultz campaign showed her leading the Democratic primary field. The New York Times is tracking polls for this race at nytimes.com/interactive/polls/florida-us-house-20-polls-2026.html. No independent general election polls were found as the primary has not yet occurred.

candidates.name: Debbie Wasserman Schultz
candidates.summary: Debbie Wasserman Schultz has served in the U.S. House since 2005, representing Florida's 25th Congressional District, and previously chaired the Democratic National Committee from 2011 to 2016. After her current district was dismantled by the 2026 redistricting map, she opted to run in the newly reconfigured 20th District, drawing criticism from Black leaders who view the seat as a historically Black-representation district. She has $2.5 million in her campaign account as of March 2026, far outpacing her primary opponents.

candidates.name: Luther Campbell
candidates.summary: Luther Campbell, widely known as 'Uncle Luke,' is the former frontman of the rap group 2 Live Crew and a free speech activist who became a community leader, youth football coach, and podcaster. He has leveraged his name recognition and personal wealth to fund his congressional campaign, positioning himself as an outsider who will fight for working families. Campbell previously ran unsuccessfully for Miami-Dade County Mayor in 2011 and has been a vocal critic of both Republican policies and the Democratic establishment.

candidates.name: Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick
candidates.summary: Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick served as the U.S. Representative for Florida's 20th Congressional District from January 2022 until her resignation in April 2026, just before the House Ethics Committee was set to consider possible expulsion after finding she committed 25 campaign finance violations. She is also under federal indictment for allegedly directing over $5 million in disaster funds to her 2021 campaign, with a criminal trial scheduled for 2027. Despite these controversies, she is seeking a return to Congress, arguing the charges are politically motivated.

candidates.name: Dale Holness
candidates.summary: Dale Holness is a former Broward County Commissioner and former Mayor of Lauderhill who previously ran for this congressional seat in the 2021 special election and 2022 Democratic primary, losing both times narrowly to Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick (by just five votes in 2022). He emphasizes his record of increasing minority and women-owned business participation in county contracts from 10% to nearly 50%. Holness advocates for preserving Black representation in the district and has been a vocal critic of Debbie Wasserman Schultz's candidacy.

candidates.name: Elijah Manley
candidates.summary: Elijah Manley is a progressive activist who has run for office several times, including bids for Broward School Board and Florida State House District 99 in 2022. He entered the congressional race earliest, in February 2025, and has focused his campaign on Medicare for All, protecting Black voting rights, and opposing the Trump administration. Manley has raised the most money among the four Black challengers to Debbie Wasserman Schultz and has called on her to run in a different district.

forecast.rationale: Florida's 20th Congressional District has a D+20 Cook PVI and is described as the only solidly Democratic district in South Florida. The race description explicitly states the Democratic primary winner is 'heavily favored' in November. The only available poll is a May 2026 internal Wasserman Schultz campaign survey showing her leading Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick 48%-16% in the Democratic primary. However, this is a single internal poll, the primary is competitive with five Democratic candidates, and no independent or general-election polling exists. Despite the contested primary, the district's strong Democratic lean (D+20) makes the general election outcome essentially predetermined regardless of the nominee. Given sparse polling and reliance on internal data, confidence is medium rather than high.
